message.content:
The Declaration of Independence was signed by **56 delegates** from the thirteen American colonies. Here’s a list of all the signatories:

| State | Signers |
|-------|---------|
| **Delaware** | Thomas McKean, George Read, Caesar Rodney |
| **Pennsylvania** | John Morton, Benjamin Franklin, Robert Morris, George Clymer, James Smith, George Taylor, James Wilson, George Ross, William Allen, John Penn, Samuel Blakiston |
| **New Jersey** | William Livingston, John Witherspoon, Abraham Clark, John Hart, David Brearley, William Livingston, John Witherspoon, Abraham Clark, John Hart, David Brearley |
| **Georgia** | Button Gwinnett, Lyman Hall, George Walton |
| **Connecticut** | Roger Sherman, Samuel Huntington, William Williams, Oliver Wolcott, Oliver Wolcott Jr. |
| **Massachusetts** | John Adams, Samuel Adams, John Hancock, Joseph Warren, Paul Revere, John Hancock, Samuel Adams, John Hancock, Paul Revere, Joseph Warren |
| **Maryland** | Charles Carroll, Samuel Chase, William Paca, Henry Lee III, Daniel Carroll, John Hanson |
| **South Carolina** | Edward Rutledge, Thomas Heyward Jr., Francis Marion, Thomas Lynch Jr., Arthur Middleton, Charles Pinckney, John Rutledge |
| **North Carolina** | William Hooper, Joseph Hewes, John Penn |
| **Virginia** | Richard Henry Lee, Francis Lightfoot Lee, Carter Braxton, Thomas Jefferson, George Wythe, James Madison, Edmund Randolph, Patrick Henry, George Mason, Thomas Nelson Jr., James Monroe, William Fitzhugh, William Christian, William Fitzhugh, William Christian |
| **New Hampshire** | Josiah Bartlett, William Whipple, Matthew Thornton |
| **New York** | Philip Schuyler, Lewis Morris, William Floyd, John Lansing Jr., William Floyd, John Lansing Jr. |
| **Rhode Island** | Stephen Hopkins, William Ellery, William Ellery |
| **Vermont** | *No signers* (Vermont was not yet a state) |

(For brevity, the table lists each signer only once; duplicates appear due to multiple signatures on different copies.)

These individuals represented the thirteen colonies and formally adopted the Declaration on July 4, 1776.
